summary: The household's income, $42,664, is about 156% of the poverty line. That puts it above the federal 130% free-meal limit, and with no SNP or TANF there is no categorical route, so on the federal tier alone the 6-year-old would get reduced-price meals. Minnesota law settles the question instead. Minn. Stat. § 124D.111, subd. 1c, requires schools in the National School Lunch Program to join the state free school meals program and to give every student one breakfast and one lunch per school day at no cost. Under subd. 1d, the state pays the gap up to the federal free rate. The engine set the meal tier to free through Minnesota's universal free school meals rule for the one K-12 child. That matches the law, so the reference of 1 holds. The consensus answer of 0 applied only the federal income test and missed the state program.
